I've been working this land for 25 years and I know what works here in Quzhou. The soil is decent, my well pump is reliable, and with my son working in the city sending some money back, I'm not in a desperate position — but I still need the farm to earn.

My 12 mu breaks down the way it always has: 8 mu in the wheat-maize rotation and 4 mu in cotton. The wheat goes in October after I rotary-till the maize stubble, and the maize goes straight in after wheat harvest — no tillage needed, saves me fuel and time. The cotton plot I'll plough deep in spring, that's what cotton needs here.

I'll use the local improved wheat variety — nothing fancy, but reliable, around 450 jin per mu when I irrigate properly. For maize I always buy hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 or whatever the seed shop has on offer, that's standard here and I've never had reason to change. Cotton I'll use hybrid Bt seed — the bollworm pressure in this county means you have to, or you're spraying constantly anyway.

Fertilizer: I base it on what my neighbors do and what I've learned myself. Wheat gets a good base of phosphorus at sowing, nitrogen in two splits. Maize gets more nitrogen, applied at sowing and topdressed at jointing. Cotton I'll push the potassium a bit more — it improves fiber quality and the market pays better for good-quality cotton.

Irrigation I manage carefully — the water table has been dropping year on year and electricity for the pump costs money. Wheat gets 3-4 waterings: pre-sowing, jointing, heading, and one at grain fill if it's dry. Maize gets 2-3. Cotton gets 4-5 since summer heat is intense here.

Cotton pesticide is the pain — aphids, spider mites, bollworm. I'll plan for 7 sprays. Wheat and maize are much lighter.
